title: Navy clarinet and lessons with Tio and others
summary: He got a clarinet in Bordeaux while in the Navy, then after 1921 took lessons from several teachers including the younger Lorenzo Tio.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: I happened to meet one of his brothers over in Bordeaux, France. Well, he had one of John's old clarinets and just had it laying up there. And I told him, I said, well, you got that horn, why don't you give it to me? You ain't using it. For sure enough, he did. And I took John's clarinet and kept it on the boat, fooling around with it, you know, in my spare time. And I came out the Navy 1921, 1920. And I played around here a while. And then finally I decided I'd take lessons and try to learn it right, you know? So, I went to old man John, I'm afraid of taking lessons from him. And I found I was making some slow improvement with him. And I left him and went to Dave Poikins.
That was on the clarinet, did you say?

On the clarinet, yeah. And after I left Dave Poikins, I went to Pinchback T-Roll. I was taking a couple of lessons from the old man Shalini. I was taking a couple of lessons from Edmund Hall. I was taking a couple of lessons from T-Roll. Tio, you remember Tio? Yeah, I didn't know him.
Yeah, I was taking a couple of lessons from him.
That was the younger Lorenzo Tio.
